_doc: MUTABLE routing table for Cortados. Edit freely: the router reloads this file when its mtime changes, no restart. Models, lanes and order WILL change; the six features and the band conditions come from the 2.0 scale (scale-2.0-reference.json). Validation on load: unknown lane/provider, a Fable/ceiling entry outside R4, or a non-Grok model on the cursor lane = file rejected, last good table kept.

workloads._doc: #132 (owner 2026-11-22): a client's x-cortados-workload header (provider, both wires). batch caps the band at R1 (core.resolve maximum_band, mirroring min_band) and the difficulty the requirement and the frontier rules read at the most R1 admits (core.band_max_D: 5), so the selection is R1's, not only the label; a trusted min_band above R1 undoes the cap and routes the call as background work (fallback band R1 when S1 is degraded, no face floor). The hard rules win: blast radius 3 (an outward effect is floored there) keeps its band, and a degraded scorer still never defaults to Claude. Unknown values are ignored with a log line.

A model being listed here does NOT place it in a band: only `candidates` does. Unplaced models wait for a task-benchmark result or Forest's ruling (no invented tiers).

tiering._doc: Forest 2026-09-21 (evening): no band lists for choosing models. Every reachable model has an index per use case (tables/model-scores.generated.json, from public benchmarks weighted by tables/use-cases.json; 100 = best published model, 0 = the average published model). Every task gets a REQUIRED index (see `selection`). Bands survive only for what they were always about: hard rules, the orchestrator and how many sub-agents. band_references fix what the knots mean; `candidates` below is only the fallback if the generated file is unreadable.
tiering._band_references: A band's reference index per use case is the LOWER of its reference models' indexes (build_tiers.py refs_index); its tier floor is the lowest reference ability. R3 + gpt-6.1-sol (owner 2026-11-23, #143): the R3 code reference was 67.0, exactly gpt-5.6-sol's code index, so gpt-6.1-sol (66.2 code, $4/1M against $8, 90.1 general against 79.6) missed R3 code by 0.8 and R3 code paid for the older, twice-as-expensive model. 0.8 points is inside the fit's noise (a ridge-shrunk logit fit, rounded to 0.1, with community nudges of several points). Adding gpt-6.1-sol changes only the R3 code reference (67.0 -> 66.2): it is above the other references on every other use case, and its overall ability is above gpt-5.6-sol's, so the R3 tier floor (the lowest reference ability) is unchanged.
tiering.refresh: weekly (Sunday night, before training) via bin/refresh-tiers.sh
tiering._live: Forest 2026-09-22: faces follow the router per turn. pre_gateway_dispatch scores with the CortadOS Router S1 service (never the 14B) and applies a one-turn model override; a degraded/slow decision leaves the configured brain in place. Set false (hot-reload) or CORTADOS_ROUTER_LIVE=0 to fall back to shadow.

selection._doc: required index for use case u = interpolation over the task's difficulty D through the knots, never below the reference of the band the hard rules put the task in (blast radius 3 / outward → Opus-class). A knot's value is the use-case index of that band's reference models (the lower of the two). All reachable models at or above the requirement qualify; the winner has the lowest cost = its GENERAL index (a heavier model is slower and burns a scarcer subscription; qualifying is by use-case index, paying is by overall weight) + scarcity_points × scarcity of the pool it draws on − expiring_bonus when that pool's headroom is about to be wiped. Spent pools are skipped. Ceiling models (general ability ≥ the R4 references) only by escalation (G112). Nothing qualifies → the strongest available model.
selection._knots: #143 (owner 2026-11-23): S1 compresses the top of the scale (it never answered 3 on ambiguity, novelty or blast radius in a week of 3,044 code and planning calls), so D was at most 9, or 10 with the outward floor, and the old R4 (D 11) and best (D 12) knots never fired. R4 now at D 9 and best at D 10, where S1's hardest answers land; R3 moves to D 8 because knots must rise strictly. D 8 now requires the R3 reference (was two thirds of the way from R2 to R3): that is the Opus-class bar gpt-6.1-sol clears on every use case.
selection._cost: cost = weight + scarcity_points × max(scarcity,0) − expiring_credit_points × underuse − capacity credit. underuse (#132, owner 2026-11-22) = the share of the pool expected to be LOST at its next reset (headroom − learned burn rate × hours to reset, core._expected_loss_pct) when the pool is underused (scarcity < 0) and its reset times are known; else max(−scarcity,0) as before (the capped scarcity sits at −1 for every comfortably underused pool and cannot tell them apart). weight = BURN: model $/1M ÷ learned pool size (tokens per % of the pool's window), normalised to 100 for the heaviest candidate (Forest 2026-09-29: pools differ ~10× in size, so price alone under-charged Claude). Falls back to price-only for pools without a learned size.
selection.r0: R0 is scored too: requirement 0, so the cheapest route wins; that is local unless a subscription window is about to expire unused.
selection._local: Owner 2026-11-13: local models are placed by a published proxy index (tables/local-models.json → model-scores.generated.json local_models), by the provider after this selection (provider/routing.py index_local): a variant whose use-case index clears required_index takes the request unless its node is busy or unavailable, because a local lane spends no quota; never outward, blast-radius-3, R3/R4 or degraded work. This holds also against a window about to expire unused (the r0 note above describes core's own ranking, where no local route is offered).
selection._same_price_band: within one lane+pool, models whose general index is within this many points are the same price class: only the strongest of them is a candidate (Gemini 3.8 Flash over 3.6 Flash; Opus and Sonnet stay separate)
selection._lane_tiebreak: equal cost → this order: local first (a tie at R0 is the reflex case), then the lane whose pool is least fought over

primary_sources._doc: Forest 2026-09-23: native subscription first; Cursor and Antigravity's Claude/GPT pool are secondary for these vendors' models and only qualify when the native pool is spent (ok=False). Cursor is primary for Grok, Composer, Kimi, GLM, Muse and anything without a native lane here.

selection._ceiling: Forest 2026-09-23: Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra WIN BY SCORE (supersedes G112 escalation-only). The requirement reaches their index at D≥9 (#143: was D≥11, which S1 never produced; a hard, high-novelty, high-ambiguity task) and any use case where only they clear the bar; their price ($20/1M Fable) keeps them off easy work. Thinking/strategy work: see the specialization file (tables/community-sentiment.json) once the nightly rating exists.
selection._sticky: a session keeps its model only while that model is within sticky_slack_points of the cheapest qualifying route; scarcity or price changes move it. Browser/desktop sessions are pinned (budgets.json stickiness) until their pool is spent.

ceiling_work._frontier: #143 (owner 2026-11-23): the R4 reference index alone did not keep this work on the frontier: gpt-6.1-sol clears it for planning (88.8 >= 87.4) and research (92.9 >= 85.9), so frontier models won 0 of 515 such calls in a week. require_frontier: only ceiling models (model-scores `ceiling`: Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Astra) qualify for it while one is available; when every frontier route is spent or refused, the index rule alone applies again (a spent frontier never blocks routing). Code joins at D >= 9 (min_D_by_use_case), not 7: D 8 code is mostly the outward floor's routine edit-and-push work (951 of 1,516 R3 calls in the audit week reached R3 only through that floor).
ceiling_work._doc: Forest 2026-09-25: Fable and Astra are what the expensive subscriptions are FOR: strategic decisions and insight. Planning and research work of at least moderate difficulty (D ≥ 5) requires the R4 reference index for that use case, so only the ceiling models clear it (Astra 100/100 on planning/research, Fable 91/90). min_D 7 (Forest 2026-09-29): an outward turn already carries blast_radius 3, so D ≥ 5 caught ordinary replies tagged planning; real strategic asks (ambiguity/novelty) clear 7. Everything else keeps the price ladder, where open and mid models take what they can. Their pools' underuse credit then decides how much of the rest they attract.

ceiling_underuse._doc: when a ceiling model's own pool is underused (scarcity ≤ −0.3: the allowance would otherwise expire unused), it also takes any R3-level task (D ≥ min_D) in every use case: paid-for capacity is used, not lost. Several underused ceiling pools: the one expected to lose the largest share at its reset wins (#132, owner 2026-11-22: rule kept, ranking by loss at reset), cost breaks ties; when any of them has no reset time, the cheapest (the earlier ranking). #143 (owner 2026-11-23): min_D 9 -> 8, because S1's compressed top puts most hard work at D 8-9; and with a conversation key (underuse_split) the spare ceiling pools share the work in proportion to the quota each would lose instead of the top one taking all of it. Routes failing the host's admission check (hold_ok: the client's quota floor) are never taken by this rule.

api_pacing._doc: Scarcity v2 §9 step 4 (owner 2026-11-24: the API credit grant is 'just like another subscription'; same models, same bands, 'just scarcity for a factor of percent used'). On: the grant's one standardized percent used is dollars spent / the stop line's dollars ($190 of a $200 grant; the scarcity reading's own %), and its pace is the rate that reaches the stop line exactly at its last counting hour, (100 - used) / hours left (core.api_pace). Its v21 'free until the grant lapses' weight discount is gone: it pays the same burn weight and cost terms as any pool. Among the underused pools of an underuse split (same gates: qualifying, available, the host's admission check, expected to lose at least min_loss_pct), its share is needed / (needed + actual pace), actual being its learned recent burn (else its window's pace so far): lagging its pace it draws more than half, ahead of it less, 1 while it has absorbed nothing; the subscription pools share the rest in their own v21 proportions. Expiry pressure is the 1 / hours left in the needed pace. The provider's 3-day expiry preference (routing.prefer_api_credit, api-credit.json prefer_within_days) is retired while this is on. Unchanged: the 95 % stop line, upper-bound reservations, the org monthly limit, the expiry cut-off, and the refusal of sensitive, local-only, outward, blast radius above 1 and degraded-scorer work. Off: routing exactly as table v21.

underuse_split._doc: #143 (owner 2026-11-23): among underused pools, selection was winner-takes-all: whichever pool had the largest underuse credit took every qualifying call until the readings moved (a 400-call sample of the audit week went 400/0 to Codex while Claude B was forecast to lose about half its week). When the cheapest qualifying route is on a pool expected to lose quota at its reset, every underused pool with a qualifying route takes part: each pool's cheapest qualifying route, weighted by the quota that pool is expected to lose (expected loss % × its capacity in tokens, core._expected_lost_tokens), and one is picked by a deterministic hash of the conversation key (core.split_pick), so a conversation always lands on the same pool for the same readings and a re-routed conversation does not flap. Pools are grouped by the window that binds them (Fable on account B shares B's all-models week with Opus on B, so B's lost quota is counted once). Takes part only: available, qualifying (index >= the requirement, and a frontier model where ceiling_work requires one), passing the host's admission check (hold_ok: the client's quota floor), with a known pool size, and expected to lose at least min_loss_pct % (a pool about to be used up is not fed work it cannot absorb). A split decision is final for the switching margin: the margin exists for cost noise, and a split picks by the conversation key on purpose. No conversation key (core.decide, Hermes without a session) -> the cheapest, as before.

api_credit_lane._doc: #143 (owner 2026-11-23): the anthropic-api credit lane (#114) is a scored candidate for normal work whenever its grant has budget left above the stop line; the provider (provider/routing.py api_lane_pairs) offers its Claude models only to a request every sensitivity detector cleared, with no x-cortados-local header, on /v1/messages, whose upper-bound cost fits under the stop line, so the lane never takes sensitive or local-only work (owner 2026-11-14). Here core refuses it for a degraded scorer (a degraded scorer never defaults to Claude), an outward effect, or S1's blast radius above max_blast_radius: the continuation gate re-checks every later turn with that same rule (no outward effect, blast radius 0-1: routing.local_admission, #114), so a conversation it could not continue is never opened on it. Its weight is 'free until the grant lapses': its burn (model $ per token ÷ the grant's dollars per %) times the share of the grant NOT expected to lapse, (1 − expected loss), so while the forecast says the grant would lapse unspent its dollars cost nothing, and the cost falls as expiry nears with credit left. The burn of this pool is never the weights' normalising reference (a $190 pool would otherwise dwarf every subscription's weight).

selection._switch_margin: #132 (owner 2026-11-22): a 1–3 point cost difference is noise from the latest usage reading (R2 flipped between Opus on account B and Sol call by call). The client's previous route in the same band stays first while it qualifies, is available and costs at most this many points more than the cheapest; otherwise the cheapest stands. Held only when the host's admission check (hold_ok: the provider's client floor) passes too. The host keeps the previous route per client (provider/routing.py remember_route). 0 turns it off.
selection._pool_size_from_pool: #143 (owner 2026-11-23): Fable had no pool size (unitcost.py's window map said 'week (fable)' while the usage screen says 'week (Fable)', so claude:fable was never learned) and fell back to a price-only weight of 177.8 with no capacity credit. Does Fable use also draw on the all-models week? The audit's scarcity history says yes: every Fable-week move of 3 points or more (25 of them) came with an all-models move of about half its size (sum 330 Fable points against 210 all-models points in the same intervals), while the all-models week moved without the Fable week in 242 intervals (270 points). So Fable draws both weeks, other models only the all-models week, and 1 % of the Fable week is about 0.5 % of the all-models week. A Fable route is therefore sized by the window that binds it (core._pool_size, the same min-headroom rule as _min_headroom_pct and _expected_loss_pct): the account's all-models week while that has less headroom (true on both accounts today), else its Fable week. The Fable week's size is the learned claude:fable when it is not a lower bound below this estimate, else ratio × the same account's all-models size (0.5, from the history above).
selection._pool_size_prior: #132 (owner 2026-11-22): unitcost.py learns tokens per 1 % from the provider's own ledger only, so direct use of the same login moves the % without adding tokens and the learned size is a LOWER BOUND (lower_bound=true). On 2026-11-22 that made Codex look like 2.67 M tokens/% against 5.44 M (Claude A) and 4.95 M (Claude B), although Codex's allowance is believed to be several times Claude's. A lower-bound learned size below this prior is raised to it; a learned size above it, or one not flagged as a lower bound, stands. codex:all = 5.63 M: the 563 M tokens/week Codex estimate recorded with the burn weight (core.resolve, Forest 2026-09-29), deliberately not the full ~10× ratio, so it only corrects the undercount and is no Codex preference. Keyed by the vendor's base pool (applies to every account of it).
selection._capacity: Forest 2026-09-26: subscriptions are not normalised (Codex > Claude > Gemini > Cursor in absolute allowance). unitcost.py learns tokens-per-percent per pool from our own samples and ledger; among pools with room (scarcity ≤ 0), the route on the pool with the most tokens left gets up to capacity_credit_points off. Re-learned every 6 h and nightly.
selection._interactive_floor: Forest: the right answer over cost. A FACE turn (unit_kind interactive) never runs on a model below this general index even at R0 — 2026-09-27 09:13 the cheapest qualifying route (gpt-oss-120b, index 0) answered Forest's 'done' in Donna's 150k-token session with leaked reasoning. Crons and sub-agents keep the full ladder.

review_policy._doc: Explicit router_review only; no automatic reviewer fan-out. Compare the actual author model, not task difficulty. Ceiling flag defines frontier vs smaller; Samantha stays in that class within a use-case index gap, Rachel switches classes. Vendor means model maker, not subscription lane. OpenAI/Anthropic are preferred reciprocal partners; use another eligible vendor if unavailable. Never relax diversity/class for scarcity.
